raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen3 Coder tool-call streaming currently buffers string parameter values until the parser sees `</parameter>` or another terminating tag.

For large string arguments, such as file-writing tools with a long `content` field, this causes the OpenAI streaming response to emit the whole argument as one large chunk instead of incremental `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments` fragments.

This PR fixes Qwen3 Coder string-argument streaming so clients can receive large tool parameters progressively.

Fixes #27005.

## Modifications

- Update `Qwen3CoderDetector` to stream string-like parameters incrementally.
- Only enable incremental streaming for schema string-like types:
  - `string`
  - `str`
  - `text`
  - `varchar`
  - `char`
  - `enum`
- Keep the existing complete-value parsing path for non-string parameters such as boolean, integer, array, and object values.
- Preserve JSON validity by:
  - emitting the JSON key and opening quote once
  - JSON-escaping each streamed string fragment
  - holding potential closing-tag prefixes across chunks
  - emitting the closing quote when the parameter terminator arrives
- Add a regression test to verify a long `content` parameter emits before `</parameter>` is received.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. This change only affects tool-call parser streaming behavior and does not change model forward logic or model outputs.

Unit tests run:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/workspace/python:/workspace/test python3 -m unittest \
  registered.unit.function_call.test_function_call_parser.TestQwen3CoderDetector.test_streaming_string_parameter_emits_before_closing_tag \
  registered.unit.function_call.test_function_call_parser.TestQwen3CoderDetector.test_streaming_single_tool_call \
  registered.unit.function_call.test_function_call_parser.TestQwen3CoderDetector.test_multiple_tool_calls \
  registered.unit.function_call.test_function_call_parser.TestQwen3CoderDetector.test_complex_array_parameter \
  registered.unit.function_call.test_function_call_parser.TestQwen3CoderDetector.test_boolean_parameter_conversion
```

Result:

```text
Ran 5 tests in 0.001s

OK
```

Also ran:

```bash
python3 -m py_compile \
  python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py \
  test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. This is a parser-only change and does not affect inference kernels, scheduling, model forward execution, or token generation speed.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

We need this fix too, in product env,such long gap causes the system to assume that the return has been interrupted.

I tested this PR against a streaming/non-streaming equivalence suite and found a backward-compatibility regression for literal `null`.

Minimal case: a tool schema explicitly declares `content` as `type: "string"`, and the model emits:

```text
<parameter=content>null</parameter>
```

The current detector's complete-value path produces JSON `null`, but this PR produces the JSON string `"null"` when the input is split one character at a time:

```text
expected: {"content": null}
actual:   {"content": "null"}
```

The same suite covers 125 combinations of values and chunk sizes, plus delimiter splits, interruption, and bounded buffering. A safer implementation must retain enough uncommitted suffix to distinguish the existing literal-null conversion before opening a JSON string.

I also have paired physical evidence for the underlying issue: for identical final 15,375-character tool arguments, the existing detector emitted 8 SSE events with a 300.893 s maximum silence, while the corrected detector emitted 2,108 events with a 16.058 s initial delay and 0.421 s maximum gap thereafter. Final tool arguments and content SHA-256 were identical.

I opened #41313 against current `main`; it only streams schema-explicit `type: "string"` parameters and adds the equivalence/interruption/buffer-bound regressions. I am happy for maintainers to choose either implementation, but the literal-null case should be fixed before merging #25246.

Thanks for the detailed compatibility findings. I have updated my existing PR #41313 (head `b239e3d6`) and rebased it onto the upstream main snapshot `fb6e6a09`.

The updated implementation incrementally emits string tool arguments while reusing the existing `_get_param_type()` helper. It covers nullable/composed string schemas without adding a conflicting helper, preserves the complete-value conversion path for arrays (including `anyOf` arrays) and other non-string types, and preserves literal `null` and single leading/trailing newline handling across chunk boundaries. It also retains a bounded suffix and does not synthesize a closing value when generation is interrupted.

Validation for this revision:
- All 23 Qwen3 Coder detector test methods pass in an isolated CPU class runner using the actual detector/schema/protocol dependencies, including 335 subcases across four tests.
- The same tests against the unmodified main detector report 44 failures, including subtest failures, exposing missing incremental delivery and open-value buffering.
- 20 CPU OpenAI-to-Anthropic streaming adapter replays pass, with final arguments matching non-streaming parsing.
- Selected Ruff checks, formatting, and diff checks pass.

These are parser/adapter checks, not a new live GPU benchmark. The full test-module import in my CPU environment is blocked by the missing Triton dependency, so full upstream CI is still needed. This change improves progressive delivery; it does not claim faster model generation.

Updated code and validation details: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41313

+    def _get_param_type(self, param_name: str, param_config: dict) -> str:
+        if param_name not in param_config:
+            return "string"
+
+        config = param_config[param_name]
+        if isinstance(config, dict) and "type" in config:
+            param_type = config["type"]
+            if isinstance(param_type, list):
+                if "string" in param_type:
+                    return "string"
+                if param_type:
+                    param_type = param_type[0]
+                else:
+                    return "string"
+            return str(param_type).strip().lower()
+
+        return "string"
+
+    def _is_streamable_string_param(self, param_name: str, param_config: dict) -> bool:
+        param_type = self._get_param_type(param_name, param_config)
+        return param_type in ["string", "str", "text", "varchar", "char", "enum"]
+
+    def _json_string_fragment(self, value: str) -> str:
+        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1]
+
+    def _ensure_streaming_param_prefix(self, calls: list[ToolCallItem]) -> None:
+        if not self.json_started:
+            calls.append(ToolCallItem(tool_index=self.current_tool_id, parameters="{"))
+            self.json_started = True
+
+        if self.current_streaming_param_prefix_sent:
+            return
+
+        param_name = self.current_streaming_param_name
+        json_key = json.dumps(param_name, ensure_ascii=False)
+        prefix = f'{json_key}: "'
+        if self.current_tool_param_count > 0:
+            prefix = ", " + prefix
+
+        calls.append(
+            ToolCallItem(
+                tool_index=self.current_tool_id,
+                parameters=prefix,
+            )
+        )
+        self.current_streaming_param_prefix_sent = True
+
+    def _find_streaming_param_terminator(self, text: str) -> Optional[tuple[int, int]]:
+        candidates = []
+        for token, token_len in [
+            (self.parameter_end_token, len(self.parameter_end_token)),
+            (self.parameter_prefix, 0),
+            (self.function_end_token, 0),
+        ]:
+            idx = text.find(token)
+            if idx != -1:
+                candidates.append((idx, token_len))
+
+        if not candidates:
+            return None
+        return min(candidates, key=lambda x: x[0])
+
+    def _held_streaming_param_suffix_len(self, text: str) -> int:
+        held = 1 if text else 0
+        for token in [
+            self.parameter_end_token,
+            self.parameter_prefix,
+            self.function_end_token,
+        ]:
+            max_len = min(len(token) - 1, len(text))
+            for suffix_len in range(max_len, 0, -1):
+                if token.startswith(text[-suffix_len:]):
+                    held = max(held, min(len(text), suffix_len + 1))
+                    break
+        return held
+
+    def _reset_streaming_param_state(self) -> None:
+        self.current_streaming_param_name = None
+        self.current_streaming_param_prefix_sent = False
+        self.current_streaming_param_seen_value = False
+        self.current_streaming_param_pending = ""
+
+    def _emit_streaming_param_value(
+        self, current_slice: str, calls: list[ToolCallItem]
+    ) -> int:
+        text = self.current_streaming_param_pending + current_slice
+        self.current_streaming_param_pending = ""
+
+        if not self.current_streaming_param_seen_value and text.startswith("\n"):
+            text = text[1:]
+
+        terminator = self._find_streaming_param_terminator(text)
+        if terminator is not None:
+            end_pos, end_token_len = terminator
+            value = text[:end_pos]
+            if value.endswith("\n"):
+                value = value[:-1]
+
+            self._ensure_streaming_param_prefix(calls)
+            if value:
+                calls.append(
+                    ToolCallItem(
+                        tool_index=self.current_tool_id,
+                        parameters=self._json_string_fragment(value),
+                    )
+                )
+                self.current_streaming_param_seen_value = True
+
+            calls.append(ToolCallItem(tool_index=self.current_tool_id, parameters='"'))
+            self.current_tool_param_count += 1
+            self._reset_streaming_param_state()
+            return len(current_slice) - (len(text) - end_pos - end_token_len)
+
+        held_len = self._held_streaming_param_suffix_len(text)
+        emit_len = max(0, len(text) - held_len)
+        if emit_len == 0:
+            self.current_streaming_param_pending = text
+            return len(current_slice)
+
+        value = text[:emit_len]
+        self.current_streaming_param_pending = text[emit_len:]
+        self._ensure_streaming_param_prefix(calls)
+        calls.append(
+            ToolCallItem(
+                tool_index=self.current_tool_id,
+                parameters=self._json_string_fragment(value),
+            )
+        )
+        self.current_streaming_param_seen_value = True
+        return len(current_slice)
+

+    def test_streaming_string_parameter_emits_before_closing_tag(self):
+        """
+        Test streaming parsing of a long string parameter before the closing tag.
+
+        Scenario: A file-writing tool streams a large string parameter over
+        several chunks and the closing parameter tag is split across chunks.
+        Purpose: Verify that the parser emits JSON string fragments as the

+            "<tool_call>",
+            "<function=write_file>",
+            "<parameter=file_path>/tmp/demo.html</parameter>",
+            "<parameter=content>",
+            "<!DOCTYPE html>\n",
+            "<html>\n",
+            "<body>hello</body>\n",
+            "</par",
+            "ameter>",
+            "<parameter=overwrite>false</parameter>",
+            "</function>",
+            "</tool_call>",
+        ]
+
+        detector = Qwen3CoderDetector()
+        collected_params = ""
+        params_before_content_close = ""
+
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            result = detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, self.tools)
+            for call in result.calls:
+                if call.parameters:
+                    collected_params += call.parameters
+            if chunk == "<body>hello</body>\n":
+                params_before_content_close = collected_params
+
+        self.assertIn('"content": "', params_before_content_close)
+        self.assertIn("<!DOCTYPE html>", params_before_content_close)
+        self.assertIn("<html>", params_before_content_close)
+        self.assertIn("<body>hello</body>", params_before_content_close)
+
+        params = json.loads(collected_params)

+        self.assertEqual(
+            params["content"],

+        )
+        self.assertEqual(params["overwrite"], False)
